It is the sum of Cost of Operating Revenue [SCOR] and Operating & Maintenance (Utility) [SDOE]. Applicable for Industrial, Property, Other Financial & Investment Trust Companies.
Cost of Revenue including Operation & Maintenance (Utility) - Total [SCREV] includes:
• Cost of Operating Revenue [SCOR]
• Operations & Maintenance (Utility) [SDOE]

Cost of Revenues excluding Depreciation [SCOGXD] represents the total value of costs of goods and services diminished by the value of depreciation and amortization reported within costs of goods sold. Applicable to Industrial, Property, Investment Trust and Other Financial companies.
Cost of Revenues excluding Depreciation [SCOGXD] includes:
• Cost of Financing-Related Operations [SCFS]
• Cost of Revenues - Total [SCGS]
• Amortization in Cost of Revenues [SACS] (deducted)
• Depreciation in Cost of Revenues [SDCS] (deducted)

Operating Expenses [SOPEX] represents the total expenses. Applicable to all Industries.
Operating Expenses [SOPEX] is the difference between:
• Revenue from Business Activities - Total [STLR]
• Earnings before Interest & Taxes (EBIT) [SEBIT]

Selling, General & Administrative Expenses excluding Research & Development Expenses [SGAXRD] represents Selling, General & Administrative expenses excluding R&D expenses. Applicable to all industries.
Selling, General & Administrative Expenses excluding Research & Development Expenses [SGAXRD] includes:
• Selling, General & Administrative Expenses - Total [SSGA]
• Less Research & Development Expense - Supplemental [SRDE]

Banks and Insurance companies additionally includes:
• Stock-Based Compensation in Research & Development Expense [ESCR]

DPS - Common - Gross - Issue - By Payable Date [SYPSGI] represents dividends per common share before taxes, disclosed per specific share issue on the day on which any declared stock dividends are due to be paid out. Applicable to all Industries.
DPS - Common - Gross - Issue - By Payable Date [SYPSGI] includes:
• Dividends Per Share - Common - Gross - Issue Specific [XDPSGI]

DPS - Common - Gross - Issue - By Ex Date [SXPSGI] represents dividends per common share before taxes, disclosed per specific share issue on the day on which a company sets as one business day before the period end date/record date. Applicable to all Industries.
DPS - Common - Gross - Issue - By Ex Date [SXPSGI] includes:
• Dividends Per Share - Common - Gross - Issue Specific [XDPSGI]

Operating Expenses excluding Non-Cash Charges - Total [SOENCC] represents the total value of operating expense minus the maximum value of combined depreciation and amortization reported by the company in the income statement, cash flow or notes. Applicable to all Industries.
Operating Expenses excluding Non-Cash Charges - Total [SOENCC] includes:
• Operating Expenses - Total [SOET]
• Depreciation & Amortization - Total [STDAE] (less)

Income Available to Common Shares before Depreciation & Amortization [SNISDA] represents total net income/loss reported by the company after provision for income taxes, equity in earnings, after-tax adjustments, discontinued operations, extraordinary items and minority interest, but before other adjustments to net income, preferred dividends and other distributions excluding the maximum value of combined depreciation and amortization. Applicable to all Industries.
Income Available to Common Shares before Depreciation & Amortization [SNISDA] includes:
• Income Available to Common Shares [SNIS]
• Depreciation, Depletion & Amortization - Total [STDAE]

Total Common & Spl DPS -Gross - Issue - By Announcement Date [STDSGI] represents dividends per common share before taxes, disclosed per specific share issue. It includes special dividends per share before taxes, paid to common shareholders on the day on which a company announces its intention to pay dividends to its shareholders. Applicable to all Industries.

Depreciation in Cost of Revenues [SDCS] represents the accounting process of allocating the cost of tangible fixed assets to expenses over those periods expected to benefit from the use of the assets. It’s the sum of depreciation reported outside of cost of sales, outside of selling, general and administrative expenses as well as outside research and development expenses. It the value of pure depreciation is not available then it’s the sum of combined values depreciation with amortization. Applicable to Industrial, Property and Investment Trust companies.
Depreciation in Cost of Revenues [SDCS] includes:
• Depreciation in Cost of Revenues [EDEC]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets in Cost of Revenues [EDLC]
• Depreciation & Amortization in Cost of Revenues [EDAC]

If any items in Cost of goods sold are reported, it will include the following items:
• Depreciation & Amortization [EDAE]
• Depreciation [EDEP]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets [EDLR]

Labor & Related Expenses including Stock-Based Compensation in Cost of Revenues [SLAC] represents labour costs reported within the cost of goods sold. This would also be populated when company uses 'by nature' presentation of the income statement (reporting material expenses, change in inventories, depreciation/amortization, labor and related expenses) and labour cost is deemed to be part of cost of revenue for manufacturing and mining companies. Applicable to Industrial, Property and Investment Trust companies.
Labor & Related Expenses including Stock-Based Compensation in Cost of Revenues [SLAC] includes:
• Labor & Related Expenses in Cost of Revenue [ELAC]
• Stock-Based Compensation in Cost of Revenue [ESCC]

Cost of Revenues - Other - Total [SCOS] represent the sum of all other costs of sales not related directly with production. Applicable to Industrial, Property and Investment companies.
Cost of Revenues - Other - Total [SCOS] includes:
• Cost of Revenues - Other [EOCG]

Industrial and Property companies additionally includes:
• Merchandise & Finished Goods - Ending Balance [EMFG] (Deducted)
• Merchandise & Finished Goods - Opening Balance [EBMF]
• Cost of Purchased Merchandise [ECPM]
• Cost of Products Manufactured [ECMA]
• Transfer from/to Other Account [ETOA]

Industrial companies additionally includes:
• External Expenses - Third Parties - Other [EOXE]
• Fuel & Oil Expense [EFOE]
• Lease Operating Expenses (Oil & Gas Industry) [ELOE]
• Airport Charges/Fees [EAPC]
• Aircraft Operating Lease Costs [EAOL]
• Aircraft Maintenance [EAMT]
• Programming Costs [EPRC]
• Network Costs [ENWC]
• Royalties/Licenses - Government [EGRL]
• Decommissioning & Rehabilitation Costs [EDRC]
• Production Expenses/Mining Costs/Cost of Sales [EPMC]
• Gaming Taxes [EGTX]

Other Operating Expense/(Income) - Net [SOIE] represents net operating expenses/income which are either not specified as being for plant hire, fixed asset rentals, depreciation/amortization, marketing, duties/taxes, exchange losses, research/development or exploration or which may represent a combination of some or all of these items. This item is adjusted by rounding adjustments. Applicable to all Industries.
Other Operating Income/Expense - Net [SOIE] includes:
• Other Operating Income - Total [SOOI] (deducted)
• Other Operating Expense [SOOE]
• Operating Provisions [SOPV]
• Non-Recurring Adjustments - Operating [SNRO] (deducted)
• Supplementary Adjustments - Operating [SSPO] (deducted)

Industrial companies additionally includes:
• Provision for Decommissioning Fund & Environmental Obligations [SPDF]

Banks additionally includes:
• Contributions & Transfer to Bank Guarantee Fund [SBGF]

Non-Recurring Adjustments - Operating - Decrease/(Increase) [SNRO] represents non-recurring adjustments disclosed by companies in a note to Operating Profit/Profit from Operations. These cannot be allocated to a specific data point within operating income/expenses and is usually disclosed as a component to arrive at Operating Profit/Profit from Operations. Applicable to all Industries.

Interest Income - Non-Bank [SINI] represents interest from investments together with any income received on short term lending. Interest received from advances, deposit accounts. Applicable to Industrial, Property, Investment and Financial companies.
Interest Income - Non-Bank [SINI] includes:
• Interest Income - Non-Bank [EIIN]
• Interest Expense on Financial Lease Liabilities [EILL]
• Interest Expense/Income - Net [EINN] (if the value is positive)
• Financial Expense - Total [XTFE] ((in the absence of pure interest income and is an Income)
• Net Financing Income/Expense [XNFI] (in the absence of pure Interest expense and Financial Income and is an Income)
• Allowance for Funds Used during Construction - Equity Portion (AFUDC) [EAFC] (additional for Industrial companies)

Interest Expense - Net of Capitalized Interest [SIEN] represents interest expense on debt, net of capitalized. Additionally this item should also be used when the company does not delineate separately gross interest costs and interest capitalized that is when the company just reports Interest expense on the face. Applicable to Industrial, Insurance, Property, Investment Trust and Other Financial companies.
Interest Expense - Net of Capitalized Interest [SIEN] includes:
• Interest Expense on Capital Financing - Gross [STIE]
• Dividends on Hybrid Financial Instruments - Liability Portion [SDHY]
• Interest Capitalized [SICA] (deducted)
• Interest Expense - Net of Capitalized Interest [EIEN]
• Interest Expense on Financial Lease Liabilities [EILL]
• Interest/Dividends on Hybrid Financial Instruments - Liability Portion [EPRD]
• Interest Expense/Income - Net [EINN] (if this is an expense)
• Financial Expense - Total [XTFE] (in the absence of pure interest expense)
• Net Financing Income/Expense [XNFI] (in the absence of pure Interest expense and Financial Expense and is expense)

Industrial companies additionally includes: 
• Allowance for Funds Used during Construction - Debt Portion (AFUDC) [SAFD]

Restructuring Charges [SRST] represents expenses or provisions associated with the reorganization of certain functions, regrouping of divisions or closing of a facility/branch. These may include the consolidation of divisions, relocation of facilities and/or employees, and employee termination costs. Applicable to all Industries.
Restructuring Charges [SRST] includes:
• Restructuring Charges & Provisions [ERES]

Litigation Expenses/Settlements [SLIT] represents non-recurring litigation expenses and legal/litigation provisions . Litigation expenses may include fees for lawyers, or the settlement of charges. However, litigation does not include standard business-related lawyers' fees. Applicable to all Industries.
Litigation Expenses/Settlements [SLIT] includes:
• Legal Provisions & Litigation Expenses [ELIT]

Unrealized Adjustments on Derivatives for Hedging [SDUA] represents the unrealized fair value changes of derivative assets held for hedging purposes. Applicable to all industries.
Unrealized Adjustments on Derivatives for Hedging [SDUA] includes:
• Unrealized Adjustments on Derivatives for Hedging [EDEO]

Fair Value Adjustments - Financial Investments [SFVI] represents fair value re-measurements of financial investments. Fair value adjustments may reflect a change to key assumptions required by accounting standards, resulting in a different valuation of financial instruments. Applicable to all Industries.
Fair Value Adjustments - Financial Investments [SFVI] includes: 
• Fair Value Adjustments - Financial Investments [EFVI]

Sale & Acquisition of Group Companies - Gain/(Loss) [SDSA] represents gain/(Loss) on sale and acquisition of subsidiaries/associated companies but not forming part of discontinued operations. Applicable to all Industries.
Sale & Acquisition of Group Companies - Gain/(Loss) [SDSA] includes:
• Sale & Acquisition of Group Companies - Gain/Loss [SDSA]
• Acquisition Cost of Group Companies [EAQA] (deducted)

Equity in Earnings/(Loss) of Affiliates (after Taxes) [SQEA] represents the share of earnings/losses that the company is entitled to from unconsolidated affiliated companies which has not been distributed as dividends. It includes the non-recurring part of profit/loss. Applicable to all Industries.
Equity in Earnings/(Loss) of Affiliates (after Taxes) [SQEA] includes:
• Equity Earnings - Net of Tax [CEIA]
• Non-Recurring Portion of Equity Earnings [SNRE]

Extraordinary Activities - after Tax - Gain/(Loss) [STEX] represents the all after tax extraordinary items reported by the company. Applicable to all Industries.
Extraordinary Activities - after Tax - Gain/(Loss) [STEX] includes:
• Discontinued Operations - Net of Taxes - Total [SDON]
• Impacts from Changes in Accounting Standards [SGAP]
• Extraordinary Items [SXTR]
• Extraordinary Items - Tax Impact [SSIT]

In the absence of the breakdown above it includes Extraordinary Items (after Tax) [XTEX].

Discontinued Operations - Net of Taxes - Total - Income/(Expense) [SDON] represent net result from current discontinued operations combined with the sale of discontinued operations, after taxes. Applicable to all Industries.
Discontinued Operations - Net of Taxes - Total - Income/(Expense) [SDON] includes:
• Discontinued Operations - Net - Income/Expense [SXCD]
• Sale of Discontinued Operations - Net - Gain/Loss [SXDD]
• Discontinued Operations before Tax [SDBT]
• Discontinued Operations - Tax Impacts [STID]

In the absence of the breakdown above it includes Discontinued Operations - Net of Taxes [XDOT].

Discontinued Operations before Tax - Total - Income/(Expense) [SDBT] represents the value of all discontinued operations reported before income tax. Applicable to all Industries.
Discontinued Operations before Tax - Total - Income/(Expense) [SDBT] includes:
• Discontinued Operations before Tax [ZDBU]

If the account above is not available, it includes:
• Discontinued Operations before Tax - Income/Expense [SDCG]
• Sale of Discontinued Operations before Tax - Gain/Loss [SDDG]

Discontinued Operations before Tax - Income/(Expense) [SDCG] represents the gross current income and expenses generated by the operations of a business unit or subsidiary available for sale, before deduction of taxes. Applicable to all Industries.
Discontinued Operations before Tax - Income/(Expense) [SDCG] includes: 
• Discontinued Operations before Tax - Income/Expense [ZCDG]

Sale of Discontinued Operations before Tax - Gain/(Loss) [SDDG] represents any gain/loss from the sale of business unit or subsidiary before deducting the tax from discontinued operational items. Applicable to all Industries. 
Sale of Discontinued Operations before Tax - Gain/(Loss) [SDDG] includes:
• Sale of Discontinued Operations before Tax - Gain/Loss [ZDDG]

Discontinued Operations - Tax Impacts [STID] represents tax on discontinued operations. Applicable to all Industries.
Discontinued Operations - Tax Impacts [STID] includes:
• Discontinued Operations - Tax Impacts - Current Income/Expense [ETDT]
• Discontinued Operations - Tax Impacts - Gain/Loss on Sale [ETDD]
• Discontinued Operations - Tax Impacts [ETID]

Minority Interest [SMNI] represents the share of earnings/losses in subsidiaries that belongs to shareholders other than the parent company when the parent company owns less than 100%, but more than 50%, of a subsidiary. Since the subsidiary's financials are consolidated by the company, this value is a negative number to represent the amount the company does not own. Applicable to all Industries.
Minority Interest [SMNI] includes:
• Minority Interest - Continuing Operations [CMIN]

If the account above is not available, it includes Minority Interest - Total [XIMI].

Distribution for Preferred Shares [SDFS] represents the total dollar amount of the current dividend requirement on issued preferred stock of a company (including its subsidiaries).  Preferred stockholders normally forgo voting rights and receive a fixed dividend that takes precedence over the payment of dividends to common stockholders. Preferred dividends are usually cumulative and non-participative in nature. When preferred stock is redeemed during the year, the company may still report preferred dividends on the income statement, although there is no preferred stock outstanding at the end of that fiscal year. Applicable to all Industries.
Distribution for Preferred Shares [SDFS] includes: 
• Distribution for Preferred Shares [CPRD]

If the account above is not available, it includes Preferred Dividends, Distributions & Earnings Adjustments - Total [XPFS] (deducted).

Other Comprehensive Income - Unrealized Investment Gain/(Loss) [SCGL] represents other comprehensive income or losses generated by the revaluation of investments which has not been accounted for in the Income Statement. Applicable to all Industries.
Other Comprehensive Income - Unrealized Investment Gain/(Loss) [SCGL] includes:
• Other Comprehensive Income - Unrealized Investment Gain/Loss - Net of Tax [XCGN]

Comprehensive Income - Attributable to Minority Interest - Total [SCIM] represents minority interest reported as part of total comprehensive income. Includes the minority share of both net income and other comprehensive income. Mainly reported under International Financial Reporting Standards.
The share of total comprehensive income in subsidiaries that belongs to shareholders other than the parent company when the parent company owns less than 100%, but more than 50%, of a subsidiary. Since the subsidiary's financials are consolidated with the company, this value is a negative number to represent the amount the company does not own. Applicable to all Industries.
Comprehensive Income - Attributable to Minority Interest - Total [SCIM] includes:
• Comprehensive Income - Attributable to Minority Interest - Total [XCIM]

Depreciation & Amortization - Supplemental [SDEA] represents the amount charged for the combined depreciation of tangible fixed assets and amortization of intangibles during the period. Applicable to all Industries.
Depreciation & Amortization - Supplemental [SDEA] includes:
• Depreciation & Amortization - Supplemental [VDAE]

If account above is not available, it includes:
• Depreciation Expense - Total - Supplemental [SDPR]
• Amortization - Total - Supplemental [SAMR]

In the absence of the breakdown above it includes Depreciation & Amortization [EDAE].

Depreciation Expense - Total - Supplemental [SDPR] represents the accounting process of allocating the cost of tangible fixed assets to expenses over those periods expected to benefit from the use of the assets. Applicable to all Industries.
Depreciation Expense - Total [SDPR] includes:
• Depreciation - Supplemental [VDEP]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets - Supplemental [VDLR]

In the absence of the breakdown above it includes:
• Depreciation in Cost of Revenues [EDEC]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets in Cost of Revenues [EDLC]
• Depreciation in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EDES]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EDLS]
• Depreciation in Research & Development Expenses [EDRD]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets in Research & Development Expenses [EDRL]
• Depreciation [EDEP]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets [EDLR]

Depreciation - Total [STDEP] represents the maximum value of depreciation reported by the company in the income statement, cash flow or notes. Applicable to all industries.
Depreciation - Total [STDEP] includes:
•Depreciation - Total [TDEP]

Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA - Company Reported [SNAE] represents earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and income taxes adjusted to exclude total stock-based compensation expense, costs incurred to spin-off, costs associated with business transformation plan, trademark royalty costs, gain or loss related to pre-spin off etc. Adjusted EBITDA differs from EBITDA in that adjusted EBITDA normalizes income and expenses since different companies may treat each type of income and expense differently. By standardizing cash flows and discounting anomalies that may occur, adjusted, or normalized, EBITDA can provide a useful measure of comparison when evaluating multiple companies. This is collected as reported by the company. Applicable to all Industries.
Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA - Company Reported [SNAE] includes:
• Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA [CNAE]

Derivatives - Hedging - Gain/(Loss) - Total - Supplemental [SGLD] represents the total value of income or losses arising from derivative assets that are held for hedging purposes. Applicable to Insurance, Bank, Investment Trust and Other Financial companies.
Derivatives - Hedging - Gain/(Loss) - Total - Supplemental [SGLD] includes:
• Unrealized Adjustments on Derivatives for Hedging - Supplemental [SUAD]
• Derivatives - Hedging - Realized Gain/(Loss) - Total - Supplemental [SDRG]
• Trading Derivatives - Gain/(Loss) - Supplemental [STDG]
• Derivatives - Hedging - Gain/Loss [EGLD]

Unrealized Adjustments on Derivatives for Hedging - Supplemental [SUAD] represents the unrealized fair value changes of derivative assets held for hedging purposes. Applicable to Industrial and Property companies.
Unrealized Adjustments on Derivatives for Hedging - Supplemental [SUAD]  includes:
• Unrealized Adjustments on Derivatives for Hedging [EDEO]

Interest Expense [SINTEX] represents Net interest expense. Applicable to all Industries
Interest Expense [SINTEX] includes:
•Interest Expense - Net of Capitalized Interest[SIEN]
•Interest Expense - Finance - Total[SIET]

Fixed Charges [SFXC] represents the sum of Interest Expense Net & Preferred Dividends adjusted to the Tax rate. Applicable to all industries.
Fixed Charges [SFXC] includes:
• Interest Expense - Net of Capitalized Interest [SIEN]
• Preferred Dividends and Similar [XPFS].

Provision for Income Tax Expense- Unclassified [SPRX] includes all taxes based on profits which are unclassified as to by region - federal, State and/or foreign government and by type - current or deferred. It also includes income taxes incurred by affiliated, associated and joint venture companies.
Provision for Income Tax Expense- Unclassified [SPRX] includes:
• Provision for Income Tax [TTAX]
• Taxes - Associated Companies [VTAC]

Tax Adjusted Operating Income [SINVC] represents Income before Discontinued Operations & Extraordinary Items adjusted to the Interest Expense Net (adjusted to Tax Rate). Applicable to all industries (Input to analytics).
Tax Adjusted Operating Income [SINVC] includes:
• Net Income after Minority Interest [SNIC]
• Interest Expense - Net of Capitalized Interest [SIEN]

Interest Expense on Capital Financing - Gross [STIE] represents interest expense on debt before interest capitalized. When not reported, it is  calculated using the gross value from the reported net and capitalized values. Applicable to Industrial, Insurance, Property, Investment and Other Financial companies.
Interest Expense on Capital Financing - Gross [STIE]  includes:
• Interest Expense on Capital Financing - Gross [ETIE]

Interest Capitalized [SICA] represents interest charges deferred to a company's property, plant and equipment account, amortized over the life of the related assets. It reflects only the portion of interest on an asset that is amortized during the fiscal period. Applicable to Industrial, Insurance, Property, Investment Trust and Other Financial companies. 
Interest Capitalized [SICA] includes:
• Interest Capitalized [ECAP]
• Allowance for Funds Used during Construction - Debt Portion (AFUDC) [SAFD]

Sale of Tangible & Intangible Fixed Assets - Gain/Loss [SFAS] represents the Income or loss on sale of fixed assets (including investment properties). Applicable to all Industries.
Sale of Tangible & Intangible Fixed Assets - Gain/Loss [SFAS] includes:
• Sale of Tangible & Intangible Fixed Assets - Gain/Loss [EGFA]
• Sale of Investment Properties - Property - Gain/Loss [ESLP]
• Sale of Leased Fixed Assets - Gain/Loss [SGLL]

Banks and Insurance additionally includes:
• Sale of Other Real Estate Owned - Gain/Loss [EORE]

Equity Earnings/(Loss) - before Taxes including Non-Recurring [SIQA] represents profits arising from any source, accounted for by the equity method. Profits or losses of subsidiaries, associated companies or other companies accounted for on the equity basis and included in Profit before tax. It includes the non-recurring portion of profits, arising from any source, accounted for by the equity method. Applicable to all Industries.
Equity Earnings/(Loss) - before Taxes including Non-Recurring [SIQA] includes:
• Equity Earnings - before Tax [EIQA]
• Non-Recurring Portion of Equity Earnings before Taxes [SNQA]

Costs Associated with IPOs & Mergers [SCAI] represents costs related to the issuance of shares and other instruments on stock exchanges, as well as the costs incurred for the acquisition of other entities. Applicable to all Industries.
Costs Associated with IPOs & Mergers [SCAI] includes:
• Costs Associated with IPOs & Mergers [ECAI]

Discontinued Operations - Net - Income/(Expense) [SXCD] represents current net income/loss generated by the operations of a business unit or subsidiary available for sale, net of tax . Applicable to all industries.
Discontinued Operations - Net - Income/(Expense) [SXCD] includes: 
• Discontinued Operations - Net - Income/Expense [ZCDN]
• Minority Interest - Discontinued Operations [CMID] (deducted)

Other Comprehensive Income - Hedging Gain/(Loss) [SCHN] represents unrealized gains or losses from hedging and risk management operations, not shown in the income statement and included in the other comprehensive income. Applicable to all Industries.
Other Comprehensive Income - Hedging Gain/(Loss) [SCHN] includes:
• Other Comprehensive Income - Hedging Gain/Loss - Net of Tax [XCHN]

Other Comprehensive Income - Pension Related [SCPP] represents pension, post-retirement and healthcare plan income or losses reported in other comprehensive income that have not been accounted for in the income statement. Applicable to all Industries.
Other Comprehensive Income - Pension Related [SCPP] includes:
• Other Comprehensive Income - Pension Liabilities - Net of Tax [XCPN]

Amortization of Computer Software - Supplemental [SASW] represents amortization of computer software for the period. Applicable to all Industries.
Amortization of Computer Software - Supplemental [SASW] includes:
• Amortization of Computer Software - Supplemental [VASW]

If the account above is not available, it includes: 
• Amortization of Computer Software [EASW]
• Amortization of Computer Software in Cost of Revenues [EASC]
• Amortization of Computer Software in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EASS]

Auditor Fees [SAFT] represents total fees for auditor services. Includes audit fees, audit-related fees, tax fees and other payments. NB: This relates to external auditors fees and do not include internal auditors fees. Applicable to all Industries.
Auditor Fees [SAFT] includes:
• Auditor Fees - Total [XAFT]

If the account above is not available, the sum of the following will be collected:
• Audit-Related Fees [SARF]
• Tax Fees [SATF]
• Fees - Other [SAOF]

Audit-Related Fees [SARF] represents all fees for professional services necessary and reasonably related to the performance an audit or review of financial statements. It also includes fees for services that are normally incurred in connection with statutory and regulatory filings or engagements, such as comfort letters, statutory audits, attest services, consents, and review of documents filed with the SEC. Applicable to all industries.
Audit-Related Fees [SARF] includes:
• Auditor Fees [VTAU]
• Audit-Related Fees  [VTAR]

Tax Fees [SATF] are fees for auditors' legal counseling services. Note: This relates to external auditors fees and does not include internal auditors fees. Applicable to all Industries.
Tax Fees [SATF] includes:
• Tax Fees [VTTF]

Fees - Other [SAOF] represents all fees paid towards other auditor services as well as other non-auditor fees. Note: This relates to external auditors fees and does not include internal auditor’s fees. Applicable to all Industries.
Fees - Other [SAOF] includes:
• Auditor Fees - Other [VTOF]
• Fees (Non-auditor) - Other [VOAF]

Revenue from Business-Related Activities - Other - Total [SOBR] represents revenue other than from sale of goods and services but still forming part of the business activities of the company. Applicable to all industries.
Revenue from Business-Related Activities - Other - Total [SOBR] includes:
Industrial:
• Revenue from Business-Related Activities - Other [ROBR]
• Islamic Income [ISIN]
• Royalty Income - Business [SROI]

Insurance:
• Revenue from Business-Related Activities - Other [ROBR]
• Revenue from Goods & Services [RNTU]
• Net Revenue/Expense - Banking Operations - Insurance [SOIB]
• Fees & Commissions Income [SCFI]

Bank:
• Revenue from Business-Related Activities - Other [ROBR]
• Revenue from Goods & Services [RNTU]

Property:
• Revenue from Business-Related Activities - Other [ROBR]
• Islamic Income [ISIN]

Investment Trust:
• Revenue from Business-Related Activities - Other [ROBR]
• Islamic Income [ISIN]
• Revenue from Goods & Services [RNTU]
• Sales of Goods & Services - Net [RNTS]

Other Financial:
• Revenue from Business-Related Activities - Other [ROBR]
• Islamic Income [ISIN]
• Revenue from Goods & Services [RNTU]

Derivatives - Hedging - Gain/(Loss) [SDHN] represents income or losses arising from derivative assets held for hedging purposes, i.e. for the purpose of limiting a company’s operating risks. The code is used when a company does not specify the precise nature of hedging income (such as realized and unrealized gains). Applicable to all Industries.
Derivatives - Hedging - Gain/(Loss) [SDHN] includes:
• Derivatives - Hedging - Gain/Loss [EGLD]

Derivatives - Hedging - Ineffective Gain/(Loss) [SDIE] represents realized gains or losses on the ineffective portion of hedging contracts. Ineffective hedging gains are those hedging results that are expensed directly in the income statement. Applicable to Industrial and Property companies.
Derivatives - Hedging - Ineffective Gain/(Loss) [SDIE] includes:
• Derivatives - Hedging - Ineffective Gain/Loss [EDIE]

Derivatives - Hedging - Realized Gain/(Loss) - Total - Supplemental [SDRG] represents the total value of realized gains or losses on the effective portion of hedging contracts.Effective hedging gains are those hedging results that were initially reported as hedging valuation result in other comprehensive income. Once the hedging contract matures or is sold, such gains or losses are expensed in the income statement. This is a specific type of realized gains/losses on hedging derivatives. Applicable to Industrial, Property and Investment Trust companies.
Derivatives - Hedging - Realized Gain/(Loss) - Total - Supplemental [SDRG] includes:
• Derivatives - Hedging - Effective Gain/(Loss) - Supplemental [SDEG]
• Derivatives - Hedging - Ineffective Gain/(Loss) - Supplemental [SDIG]
• Early Termination of Derivatives - Hedging - Gain/(Loss) - Supplemental [SDTG] 
• Derivatives - Hedging - Realized Gain/Loss [EDRG]

Derivatives - Hedging - Ineffective Gain/(Loss) - Supplemental [SDIG] represents realized gains or losses on the ineffective portion of hedging contracts.  Applicable to Industrial and Property companies.
Derivatives - Hedging - Ineffective Gain/(Loss) - Supplemental [SDIG] includes:
• Derivatives - Hedging - Ineffective Gain/Loss [EDIE]

Lease Expense -Total [SVLET] represents the total amount of lease cost recognized by lessee for lease contract. The data item is disclosed under the lease footnote. Applicable to all industries.
Lease Expense - Total [SVLET] includes:
• Lease Expense -Total [VLET]
If the account above is not available, the sum of the following will be collected:
• Operating /Rental Expense – Supplemental [SVRXP]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease ROU Assets - Supplemental [SVDLR]
• Amortization of Financial Lease ROU Assets - Supplemental [SVALR]
• Variable Lease Expense - Unclassified – Supplemental [SVLEU]
• Variable Operating Lease Expenses - US GAAP - Supplemental [SVOLE]
• Variable Financial Lease Expenses – Supplemental [SVFLE]
• Interest Expense on Financial Lease Liabilities – Supplemental [SVIFL]
• Short-Term Lease Cost – Supplemental [SVSLC]
• Sublease Income – Supplemental [SVSLI]

Operating/Rental Expense – Supplemental [SVRXP] Represents rental expenses paid for offices, factories, machinery and equipment. It includes rent for operating leasing machinery/equipment. This is collected when it is reported in notes to the financial statement and which cannot be directly or indirectly associated with the face item.

Variable Operating Lease Expenses - US GAAP [SVOLE] represents the portion of the payment made by a lessee to the lessor for the right to use an asset during the lease term that varies due to change in factors or circumstances at the commencement date of the lease. Variable Lease expense is dependent on an index or rate such as customer price index, interest rate or market rental rates. Amount of variable lease cost is recognized when obligation for payment is incurred for operating leases reported under US GAAP. Applicable to all industries.

Depreciation in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [SDES] represents the accounting process of allocating the cost of tangible fixed assets to expenses over those periods expected to benefit from the use of the assets. This represents all depreciation (pure value or combined with amortization) reported within the selling, general and administrative expenses. Applicable to all Industries.  
Depreciation in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [SDES] includes:
• Depreciation in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EDES]
• Depreciation & Amortization in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EDAS]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EDLS]
• Depreciation in Research & Development Expenses [EDRD]
• Depreciation & Amortization Expense in Research & Development Expenses [EDAR]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets in Research & Development Expenses [EDRL]

If there is no Cost of sales, this will also includes:
• Depreciation & Amortization [EDAE]
• Depreciation [EDEP]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets [EDLR]

Amortization of Intangibles in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [SAMS] represents the accounting process of allocating the cost of assets that lack physical existence over those periods expected to benefit from the use of these assets. These assets usually have a high degree of uncertainty concerning future benefits. EAMS represents the amortization of all intangible assets (including goodwill) reported within selling, general or administrative expenses. Applicable to all Industries.
Amortization of Intangibles in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [SAMS] includes:
• Amortization of Intangibles including Goodwill in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EAMS]
• Amortization of Goodwill in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EAGS]
• Amortization of Deferred Charges in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EADS]
• Amortization of Intangibles excluding Goodwill in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EAMY]
• Amortization of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EAUS]
• Amortization of Licenses, Copyrights, Property Rights & Designs in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EALS]
• Amortization of Computer Software in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EASS]
• Amortization of Brands, Patents, Trademarks, Marketing & Artistic Intangibles in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EABS]
• Amortization of Capitalized Research & Development in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EARS]
• Amortization excluding Goodwill in Research & Development Expenses [EARD]

If Cost of sales is not available, then it also includes the items below:
• Amortization of Intangibles including Goodwill [EAMI]
• Amortization of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets [EALR]
• Amortization of Intangibles excluding Goodwill [EAMO]
• Amortization of Deferred Charges [EAMD]
• Amortization of Goodwill [EAMA]
• Amortization of Licenses, Copyrights, Property Rights & Designs [EAML]
• Amortization of Computer Software [EASW]
• Amortization of Brands, Patents, Trademarks, Marketing & Artistic Intangibles [EAMB]

Rental Expense [SRXP] represents operating lease/rental expenses reported outside the cost of goods sold. Applicable to all industries. 
Rental Expense [SRXP] includes: 
• Rental Expense [ERXP]

Other Operating Expense [SOOE] represents any other operating expenses which are not specifically collected under the available granular FCC’s like Selling/General/Admin. Expense [ESGA], Operations & Maintenance (Utility) [EDOE], Other SGA [ESGO], Other Operating Income/Expenses [EOIE]. It is usually reported by the company as “Other”.  Applicable to all Industries.
• Other Operating Expense [EOOE]
• Depreciation [EDEP*]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets [EDLR*]
• Depreciation & Amortization [EDAE*]
• Amortization of Intangibles including Goodwill [EAMI*]
• Amortization of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets [EALR*]
• Amortization of Intangibles excluding Goodwill [EAMO*]
• Amortization of Deferred Charges [EAMD*]
• Amortization of Goodwill [EAMA*]
• Amortization of Licenses, Copyrights, Property Rights & Designs [EAML*]
• Amortization of Computer Software [EASW*]
• Amortization of Brands, Patents, Trademarks, Marketing & Artistic Intangibles [EAMB*]
• Depreciation - Investment Property [EDEI*]
• Other Operating Income/Expense [EOIE] (if an expense)

*The accounts are included if there are no Cost of sales, Selling, general and administrative expenses available.

Industrial and Property companies additionally includes:
• Reimbursed Costs [EORC]

Non-Recurring Adjustments - Non-Operating - Decrease/(Increase) [SNRN] represents non-recurring adjustments disclosed by companies in a note either to Pretax Profit/Profit before Taxation or not pointing to any subtotal in the Income Statements. These cannot be allocated to a specific data point within the Income Statements and are treated as a component to Non-Operating Income/Expenses. Applicable to all Industries.

Impairment - Goodwill [SIGO] represents a non-recurring item related to the unexpected and unplanned value write-down of company acquisition costs (goodwill). These assets are retained by the reporting company. Applicable to all industries.
Impairment - Goodwill [SIGO] includes:
• Impairment - Goodwill [EIGO]

Income Taxes - Other (KFAS/NLST) - Current [SCTO] represents the portion of a company’s current income tax provision not classified as Income Taxes - Domestic - Current [VCTD], Income Taxes - Foreign - Current [VCTF] or Income Taxes - Local - Current [VCTL]. This value is obtained from the notes of the financial statements. Applicable to all industries.
Income Taxes - Other (KFAS/NLST) - Current [SCTO] includes:
• Income Taxes - Other (KFAS/NLST) - Current [VCTO]
• Final Tax [FTAX]

Income Taxes - Other - Deferred [SDTO] represents the portion of a company’s deferred income tax provision not classified as Income Taxes - Domestic - Deferred [VDTD], Income Taxes - Foreign - Deferred [VDTF] or Income Taxes - Local - Deferred [VDTL]. This value is obtained from the notes of the financial statements. Applicable to all industries.
Income Taxes - Other - Deferred [SDTO] includes:
• Income Taxes - Other - Deferred [VDTO]

Depreciation - Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets - Supplemental [SDLR] represents total depreciation and amortization of the capitalized right to control the use of property, plant and equipment held under financial (capital) lease contracts. Applicable to all industries.
Depreciation - Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets - Supplemental [SDLR] includes:
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets [VDLR]
In the absence of the above it inclues
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets [EDLR]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [EDLS]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets in Cost of Revenues [EDLC]
• Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets in Research & Development Expenses [EDRL]

Labor & Related Expenses - Total [SLAR] represents the total value of all labour related expenses. It includes tax benefits relating to Stock option compensation and provisions for Stock Option compensation. Labor & Related Expense consists of expenses paid to employees of a company in the form of salaries, wages, fees, benefits or any other form of compensation. Applicable to all Industries.
Labor & Related Expenses - Total [SLAR] includes:
• Labor & Related Expenses - Supplemental [VLAR]

If the account above is not available, it includes:
• Labor & Related Expenses in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [ELAS]
• Labor & Related Expenses in Cost of Revenue [ELAC*]
• Labor & Related Expenses in Research & Development [ELRD]
• Management Remuneration [EMEN]
• Workers' Profits Participation & Welfare Funds [EWPF]
• Stock-Based Compensation in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [ESCS*]
• Stock-Based Compensation in Cost of Revenue [ESCC*]
• Stock-Based Compensation in Research & Development Expense [ESCR*]

If Stock-based compensation accounts above are not available, it includes:
• Stock-Based Compensation Expense - Pre-tax - Supplemental [VSCP]
• Stock-Based Compensation Expense - Net of Tax - Supplemental [VSCN] (second option)
• Stock-Based Compensation - Tax Benefit - Supplemental (third option)

Stock option will only be included if we have Labor and related expenses available.

Labor & Related Expenses - Supplemental [SVLAR] consists of expenses paid to employees of a company in the form of salaries, wages, fees, benefits or any other form of compensation. Applicable to all Industries.
Labor & Related Expenses - Supplemental [SVLAR] includes:
• Labor & Related Expenses - Supplemental[VLAR]

If the account above is not available, it includes:
• Labor & Related Expenses in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [ELAS]
• Labor & Related Expenses in Cost of Revenue [ELAC]
• Labor & Related Expenses in Research & Development [ELRD]
• Management Remuneration [EMEN]
• Workers' Profits Participation & Welfare Funds [EWPF]
• Stock-Based Compensation in Selling, General & Administrative Expenses [ESCS]
• Stock-Based Compensation in Cost of Revenue [ESCC]
• Stock-Based Compensation in Research & Development Expense [ESCR]

Non-GAAP Income from Operations - Company Reported [SNOG] represents income from operations calculated in accordance with GAAP as adjusted for the impact of depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation benefit or expense, impairment charges, restructuring charge or credit and other special items. Companies use different terminologies such as Non-GAAP, Adjusted, Underlying, Core & Non-IFRS to report Non-GAAP measures. This is collected as reported by the company. Applicable to all Industries.
Non-GAAP Income from Operations - Company Reported [SNOG] includes:
• Non-GAAP Income from Operations[CNGO]

Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Earnings - Company Reported [SNAN] represents net earnings calculated in accordance with GAAP as adjusted for the impact of stock based compensation and other special items less related tax effects as well as net income/loss from discontinued operations.  Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Earnings are an alternative method used to measure the earnings of a company, and many companies report non-GAAP earnings in addition to their earnings as calculated through generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). Some managers believe that these alternate figures provide a more accurate measurement of the company's financial performance. Companies use different terminologies such as Non-GAAP, Adjusted, Underlying, Core & Non-IFRS to report Non-GAAP measures. This is collected as reported by the company. Applicable to all Industries.
Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Earnings - Company Reported [SNAN] includes:
• Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Earnings [CNAN]

Non-GAAP EPS Diluted - Company Reported [SNED] represents non-GAAP diluted EPS reported by the company. The company may sometimes report different flavors of EPS like non-GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations, non-GAAP diluted EPS from discontinuing operations or non-GAAP diluted EPS but we should always collect bottom line EPS to this field i.e. collect diluted non-GAAP EPS including extraordinary items to this field. This is collected as reported by the company. Applicable to all Industries.
Non-GAAP EPS Diluted - Company Reported [SNED] includes:
• Non-GAAP EPS Diluted [CNED]

Non-GAAP Operating Margin % - Company Reported [SNGM] represents non-GAAP income from operations divided by revenues. It includes operating profit calculated as per GAAP as adjusted for the impact of business disposals, acquisition and disposal related costs, impairments and other one-off items.   Companies use different terminologies such as Non-GAAP, Adjusted, Underlying, Core & Non-IFRS to report Non-GAAP operating margin. This is collected as reported by the company. Applicable to all Industries.
Non-GAAP Operating Margin % - Company Reported [SNGM] includes:
• Non-GAAP Operating Margin % [CNGM]

Reported - Tax Impact from Non-Recurring Items - Non-GAAP [SCRTI] represents the as reported tax impact on non-GAAP non-recurring items. Governing financial bodies require companies to report according to GAAP principles, the uniformity of which allows users to make comparisons with other companies in the same industry. Additionally, companies are allowed to report alternative or non-GAAP measures which provide the user with additional information on the company’s performance. When presenting non-GAAP financial information companies are required to disclose the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure as well as a reconciliation of the non-GAAP financial measure to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure. Applicable to all industries. 
Reported - Tax Impact from Non-Recurring Items - Non-GAAP [SCRTI] includes:
• Reported - Tax Impact from Non-Recurring Items - Non-GAAP [CRTI]

Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets [SVDLR] represents the total depreciation or amortization of the capitalized right to control the use of property, plant and equipment held under financial (capital) lease contracts. It is collected when the total value is reported in the notes and cannot be directly or indirectly associated to any item on the face of the income statement. It is not collected if component values are already collected in their specific FCCs. Applicable to all industries.
Depreciation of Financial Lease Right-of-Use Assets [SVDLR] includes:
• The total depreciation or amortization of the right to use property, plant and equipment held under financial (capital) leases
• The total depreciation of tangible assets held under leasing contracts reported in the International Financial Reporting Standards

Interest Expense on Financial Lease Liabilities - Supplemental [SVIFL] represents the interest expense on financial (capital) leases. The data item is disclosed under the lease footnote. Applicable to all industries.
Interest Expense on Financial Lease Liabilities [SVIFL] includes:
• Interest on right-of-use liabilities 
• Amortization of financial lease liabilities.
Short-Term Lease Cost [SVSLC] represents amount of short-term lease cost for lease with term within one year. The data item is disclosed under the lease footnote. Applicable to all industries.
Sublease Income [SVSLI] represents amount of sublease income excluding finance and operating lease expense. The data item is disclosed under the lease footnote. Applicable to all industries.

Supplementary Adjustments - Operating - Decrease/(Increase) [SSPO] represents targeted data items disclosed by companies in the notes to the accounts but cannot be assigned to any item presented within the Income Statement. These items are deemed to be part of operating income/expenses and adjusted in here to ensure the item can be shown in its respective position and the statement is still balancing. Applicable to all Industries.

Sale of Investments Held for Sale, Maturity & Trading - Gain/(Loss) [SGIT] represents realized gains and losses on the sale of investments held for sale, maturity and trading. Applicable to Industrial, Property, Investment and Financial companies.
Sale of Investments Held for Sale, Maturity & Trading - Gain/(Loss) [SGIT] includes:
• Sale of Investments Held for Sale, Maturity & Trading - Gain/Loss [EGIT]

Impairment - Intangibles excluding Goodwill [SIIO] represents a non-recurring item related to the unexpected and unplanned value write-down of intangibles other than goodwill. These assets are retained by the reporting company. Applicable to all Industries.
Impairment - Intangibles Excluding Goodwill [SIIO] includes:
• Impairment - Intangibles excluding Goodwill [EIIO]

Extraordinary Items [SXTR] represents events and transactions that are distinguished by their unusual nature, by the infrequency of their occurrence, and the materiality of their impact on the earnings of the company, reported after income taxes.  Applicable to all Industries.
Extraordinary Items [SXTR] includes:
• Extraordinary Items [XTRA]
• Income Taxes - Non-Recurring Tax Change Impact [VTXC] (deducted)
• COVID-19 Income Taxes - Non-Recurring Charge/(Credit) [SCXC] (deducted)

Non-GAAP EPS Basic - Company Reported [SNEB] represents non-GAAP basic EPS reported by the company. The company may sometimes report different flavors of EPS like non-GAAP basic EPS from continuing operations, non-GAAP basic EPS from discontinuing operations or non-GAAP basic EPS but we should always collect bottom line EPS to this field i.e. collect basic non-GAAP EPS including extraordinary items to this field. This is collected as reported by the company. Applicable to all Industries.
Non-GAAP EPS Basic - Company Reported [SNEB] includes:
• Non-GAAP EPS Basic [CNEB]

Non-Recurring/Unusual Items - Tax Impact [SCRTU] represents the as reported tax impact on unusual items. Applicable to all industries.
Non-Recurring/Unusual Items - Tax Impact [SCRTU] includes:
• Non-Recurring/Unusual Items - Tax Impact [CRTU]

Provision for Decommissioning Fund & Environmental Obligations [SPDF] represents provision for the decommissioning of mines or other natural assets used in the operations of the company to extract natural resources after their full utilization. Applicable to Industrial companies. 
Provision for Decommissioning Fund and Environmental Obligations [SPDF] includes: 
• Provision for Decommissioning Fund & Environmental Obligations [EPDF]

DPS - Common - Gross - Issue - DR - By Announcement Date [SDPSGIDR] represents dividends per common share before taxes, disclosed per specific share issue on the day on which a company announces its intention to pay dividends to its shareholders. Applicable to all industries.
DPS - Common - Gross - Issue - DR - By Announcement Date [SDPSGIDR] includes:
• Dividends Per Share - Common - Gross - by Declaration Date [DPSCDD] (Divided by DR ratio)
• Dividends Per Share - Common - Gross - Issue Specific [XDPSGI] (Divided by DR ratio)

DPS - Common - Net - Issue - DR - By Announcement Date [SDPSNIDR] represents represents dividends per common share after taxes, disclosed per specific share issue on the day on which a company announces its intention to pay dividends to its shareholders. Applicable to all industries. 
DPS - Common - Net - Issue - DR - By Announcement Date [SDPSNIDR] includes:
• DPS - Common - Net - Issue - By Announcement Date [SDPSNI] (Divided by DR ratio)

Provision for Income Tax by Region - Total [SPAX] includes all taxes based on profits that may be owed to federal, State and/or foreign government. These taxes do not include regressive taxes, such as sales taxes or excise taxes to state and federal government. It includes income taxes incurred by affiliated, associated and joint venture companies. Applicable to all Industries.
Provision for Income Tax by Region - Total [SPAX] includes:
• Income Taxes - Other (by Region) [SITO]
• Income Taxes - Foreign [SITF]
• Income Taxes - Domestic [SITD]

Income Taxes - Domestic [SITD] represents any tax provision attributable to its local tax jurisdictions segmented by geographic location of tax jurisdiction. This value is obtained from the notes of the financial statements. Applicable to all industries.  Income Taxes - Domestic [SITD] includes:
• Income Taxes - Domestic (by Region) [VTDT]
• Income Taxes - Local (by Region) [VTLT]

Income Taxes - Foreign [SITF] represents income taxes payable in specific foreign jurisdictions. When a company reports its tax provision segmented by geographic location of tax jurisdiction, any tax provision attributable to non-domestic tax jurisdictions is classified as Income Taxes - Foreign [SITF]. This value is obtained from the notes of the financial statements. Applicable to all Industries.
Income Taxes - Foreign [SITF] includes:
• Income Taxes - Foreign (by Region) [VTFT]
